title: Development of an In Vitro Ocular Platform to Test Contact Lenses
protocol: Design eye models according to average physiological dimensions of human adult eyes.
Leave a gap of 250 µm between the eyeball and the eyelid pieces in the model.
Use computer-aided design (CAD) software to create molds.
Create new .cad file or .sldprt file with AutoCAD or Solidworks.
Design 3D models of the human eyeball/eyelid using CAD software.
Save the molds as .stl files after designing.
Import .stl files into 3D printer software such as makeware for replicator2.
Specify parameters of the print including location, sparseness, scale, orientation, and smoothness.
Save the file as a G-code file for 3D printers to read.
Select materials like PLA (polylactic acid), ABS (acrylonitrile butadiene styrene), PC (polycarbonate), or combinations thereof, to print molds.
Install desired filament of the material chosen.
Import the G-code file into the 3D printer to read.
Print the mold using the 3D printer.
Open the CNC software interface connected to a cutting drill.
Construct 3D molds according to front, top, side, and perspective views of the eyeball/eyelid model in control software.
Select appropriate parameters for machining (bit size, substrate material, material thickness).
Proceed to cut the mold using the selected parameters.
Measure 10 ml volume of PDMS base and fill it into a centrifuge tube.
Add 10% w/v elastomer solution by total weight of PDMS.
Mix the PDMS and elastomer solutions well with a stirring rod.
Pour the PDMS solution into eyeball and eyelid molds.
Allow PDMS to settle at room temperature overnight or for at least 12 hours.
Put the molds into an oven at 75 °C for 1 hour, or at 150 °C for 5 minutes.
Put the samples in a freezer for a few minutes.
Extract the eyepieces from the molds using a thin spatula.
Connect a 1/16" x 1/8" polytetrafluoroethylene tube with a 1/16" equal leg coupler tube connector.
Attach the connected tubing to the eyelid piece at the tubing hole.
Measure 2 g of agarose and mix with 100 ml of ultrapure water.
Bring the solution to a boil (100 ºC) until the agarose dissolves completely.
Let the solution cool down for 5 min.
Pour the solution into the eyeball mold.
Allow the solution to cool for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the eyeball pieces with a spatula.
Store the eyeball agar in a -20 °C freezer for later use.
Turn the flow hood on for 10 min prior to use.
Sanitize the flow hood with 70% ethanol alcohol.
Autoclave all materials and instruments at 273 °F/133 °C for 45 min.
Immerse the bovine eye in a beaker containing diluted povidone-iodine solution for 2 min.
Rinse the eye in a beaker containing phosphate buffered saline (PBS) pH 7.4.
Place the eye on a glass petri dish with the corneal face up using forceps.
Cut excess muscle and fatty tissue at scleral attachment points with blunt end dissection scissors.
Dispose of excess tissue into a sterile beaker designated for animal waste.
Remove the conjunctiva from the eye using micro-scissors.
Wrap the eye with sterile gauze, maintaining a distance of at least 1 cm from the limbus.
Incise the sclera approximately 2 mm from the limbus region using a scalpel.
Extend the incision by 360° using a scalpel or dissection scissors without deforming the cornea.
Remove the cornea from the eye with fine forceps.
Carefully remove any adhering uveal tissue and rinse cornea with PBS.
Store the cornea at 31ºC in a sterile container with culture medium containing 3% Fetal Bovine Serum.
Design and manufacture the blink platform using CAD and 3D printing, similar to that described for the eye model (section 1.1).
Design the gear system such that it translates simple rotation of motors into the lateral and rotational motions of the eyepieces.
Using the pinion and gear mechanism, translate rotational motion of a stepper motor into the lateral motion of a pinion, which is connected to the eyelid pieces.
Using the conjugate gear system, amplify one rotational motion from a stepper motor into three (or more) rotational motions for three different eyeball pieces.
Align the two gear systems, one for the eyelid and one for eyeball, so that the distance between the two are constant.
Assemble the electronic system with a microcontroller, motor shield, and two motors.
Program the system to control motor parameters such as rounds per minute (RPM), number of rounds forward, number of rounds backward, and turning style.
Download the system software from the manufacturers' website.
Install the software and open it.
Write the code to control stepper motors in the desired configuration.
Connect the system with a source to power the electronic system so that the motors move in the desired manner as defined by the researcher.
Take the synthesized eyeball and eyelid pieces and slip them onto their corresponding clip-ons for the eye-model.
Connect the tubing that is joined with a syringe and positioned on the microfluidic pump with the eyelid piece.
Test run the platform and check for consistent movement.
Prime the tubing and check for a steady flow of artificial tear solution (ATS).
Manually move the eye-model parts together on a level plane, such that the eyeball and the eyelid are in contact.
Set the flow rate of the microfluidic pump to desired values.
Start the pump and the actuators to begin experiment.
For drug delivery experiments, place the drug-containing contact lens on the eyeball piece.
Allow the flow-through fluid to drip into a 12-well plate.
Quantify the analyte or drug concentration at desired set time intervals using UV-Vis spectroscopy or fluorescence.
Place the contact lens on the "eyeball" piece for studies evaluating tear component deposition.
Collect and discard the flow-through fluid as needed.
Remove the contact lens from the eyeball piece after the desired time intervals.
Prepare the contact lens for further analysis such as confocal microscopy.
